summary: Steingrímur Bjarnason Thorsteinsson worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Menntaskólinn í Reykjavík and the University of Copenhagen (~1851–1863), later teaching at Menntaskólinn í Reykjavík as a teacher (1872) and senior teacher (1895).

Stella Kramrisch specialized in Indology and art history, earning her Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Josef Strzygowski and Max Dvořák. She held posts at Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, the Courtauld Institute, the University of Pennsylvania, and NYU.
Stella Sandahl is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Armand Minard. She held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1984).

Sten Konow was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oslo, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (Ph.D.), and Berlin under Richard Pischel, Albrecht Weber, and others. He held professorships at Oslo and Hamburg.

Stephan Licha specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London in 2012, held postdoctoral posts at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo, and joined the University of Chicago faculty (attested 2026).
Stephan Marcus Salzberg studied Sinology and Buddhist studies at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephan V. Beyer works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Rochester and under Richard Hugh Robinson, served as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1972–1979), and held a post at Sidley Austin.

Stephanie Kaza is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Oberlin, Stanford, Starr King, and UC Santa Cruz. She studied under Thich Nhat Hanh and Joanna Macy, and was a faculty member at the University of Vermont (1991–2015).
Stephanie Roemer is a Tibetologist who completed her doctoral studies under Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist and linguist who earned her doctorate at Yale under Stanley Insler and Warren Crawford Cowgill. She taught at Harvard and became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-Iranian Linguistics at UCLA in 2002.

Stephen Addiss was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan. He held professorships at the University of Kansas (1977–1992) and the University of Richmond (1992–2013).

Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied with teachers including Satya Narayan Goenka, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim. He directed Sharpham College (~1992–2000) and joined Bodhi College's core faculty (~2015).

Stephen C. Berkwitz is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned his B.A. at the University of Vermont and Ph.D. at UC Santa Barbara. In 1999, he was appointed Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Missouri State University.

Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religion. Educated at Oberlin and Princeton (Ph.D.) under Alan Sponberg, Denis Twitchett, and Daniel L. Overmyer, he has taught at Princeton University since ~1988.

Stephen Fuchs was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Wilhelm Schmidt and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Vienna. He taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and directed the Institute of Indian Culture.

Stephen G. Covell is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religion who completed his doctoral studies at Princeton University under Jacqueline I. Stone (~1995–2001). He joined Western Michigan University around 2003.
Stephen H. Phillips is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who served as a professor of philosophy and later professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 1999 and 2026).
Stephen Harris is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of New Mexico in 2014 and became an assistant professor at Leiden University that same year.

Stephen Hislop was an Indologist and linguist who earned an M.A. from the University of Edinburgh (~1834–1838), attended the University of Glasgow (~1838–1840), and studied under Thomas Chalmers (~1840–1843).

Stephen J. Laumakis is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Notre Dame (1985–1991). In 1990, he joined the philosophy department at the University of St. Thomas.
